title: Working with HTTP APIs

spans.text: WHY USE THIS?
An HTTP client exchanges requests and responses with another service; handle timeouts, status codes, and response format.
CORE EXPLANATION
Check HTTP status, headers, and body separately. External APIs can be slow or unavailable; set timeouts, bound response sizes, and validate returned JSON.
EXAMPLE CODE
QUESTION: What will this code print? Predict first, then run it.

spans.code:
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from threading import Thread
from urllib.request import urlopen

class HealthHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(self):
        self.send_response(200)
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(b'healthy')
    def log_message(self, format, *args):
        pass

server = ThreadingHTTPServer(('127.0.0.1', 0), HealthHandler)
thread = Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
thread.start()
try:
    url = f'http://127.0.0.1:{server.server_port}/health'
    with urlopen(url, timeout=2) as response:
        print(response.status, response.read().decode())
finally:
    server.shutdown()
    thread.join()
    server.server_close()

spans.title: Watch out
spans.text: Network responses can be slow or untrusted; validate external API data before using it.
COMMON MISTAKES
Set HTTP timeouts and check statuses; distinguish 401/403 and 4xx/5xx in API behavior.
